clue.text: Wine from cold picnic baskets

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hampers are lidded wicker baskets for carrying a picnic

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine is pulled out of the chilled picnic baskets on a summer outing.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAMPERS is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term is an informal name for champagne, a sparkling French drink, so it is one kind of the general category.

clue.text: American’s crisp about two Republicans, you heard, in tweet

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound, so the pronoun is replaced by the letter that sounds identical
about means going round, so the American snack wraps itself around the other pieces

blocks.note: what the British call a crisp, Americans call a chip
R is the abbreviation for Republican, doubled
the letter U is pronounced exactly like the word you

explanation.surface: Someone tweets online about American snack food and a pair of Republican politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweet looks like a social media post, but it is the bird sound; the British crisp is what Americans call a chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is the short high call of a small bird, and a tweet is exactly that sound.

clue.text: Tech company’s smartphone product — article from Paris

blocks.note: an app is a program you install on a smartphone
le is a French word for the, the definite article

explanation.surface: A tech firm launches a phone feature, and a French newspaper writes it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The American firm behind the iPhone and Mac computers is one of the best-known technology businesses in the world.

clue.text: Desperate Dan implores Bob, Eve and Anna, say

indicators.note: someone desperate is in a wild, disordered state, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic man called Dan pleads with three friends, Bob, Eve and Anna.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob, Eve and Anna look like people Dan is begging; they are examples of words that read the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of those names reads identically forwards and backwards, so they are examples of that kind of symmetrical word.

clue.text: Cancel and rue heartless toll

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is taken out, so only the outside letters of the word stay

blocks.note: the word rue with its central letter dropped
to toll a bell is to ring it, and a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Someone wants to scrap a road charge and regrets ever paying it.
explanation.walkthrough: Toll looks like a road charge, but here it is the sound of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke it formally, which means to annul or withdraw it.

clue.text: Maybe Sean Connery’s caught coming in drunk

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the cricket letter goes inside the word for a drunkard

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
c stands for caught on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A famous film star is arrested as he stumbles home drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Connery was born in Edinburgh; maybe signals he is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor was a famous Scottish-born man, so he is an example of a native of Scotland.

clue.text: One enters grand residence in part of Spain

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the numeral goes into the word for the stately home

blocks.note: a castle is a grand fortified home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A visitor walks into a stately home somewhere in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile is a historic region and former kingdom in central Spain, home to Madrid.

clue.text: Hot pants and new, good underwear

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the preceding word is treated as nonsense and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A clothes shop sells hot pants and stylish new underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot pants reads as one garment; in fact pants is the signal, British slang for poor or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy undergarment with a narrow strip at the back, worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Troublemaker with extremely evil urge

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
the two end letters of evil

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker feels a very wicked impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or push them to act, which is to urge them on.

clue.text: Spanish artist’s image — like so

blocks.note: pic is short for picture
as means like, in the same way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a Spanish painter's picture by making a shape with their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, born in Málaga, was a painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Act out a bit of verse in tragedy

indicators.note: out suggests something not in its proper place, so the preceding word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
a strophe is a stanza, a section of a poem

explanation.surface: An actor performs a section of poetry in a stage tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Act out and tragedy both suggest theatre, but tragedy here means a real-life calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden disaster, and a tragedy in everyday use is just such a terrible event.

clue.text: Tips for raw oysters, even caviar?

indicators.note: the tips of words are their front ends, so just the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A waiter suggests how to serve raw oysters, perhaps topped with something fancier.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits caviar is just one example of the fish eggs in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is salted sturgeon eggs, an example of fish eggs in general.

clue.text: Disaster narrowly avoided on earth in giant houses

indicators.note: a house holds something within it, so the answer sits inside the run of words before it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of on to the start of giant

explanation.surface: A catastrophe on Earth was barely averted, perhaps a huge asteroid's near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, a situation where calamity almost happened but did not.

clue.text: Dad’s attempt to make a flan, say

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive s
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A father tries his hand at baking a flan.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open tart with a baked crust, so it is an example of a baked dough dish.

clue.text: Perhaps some beer gives you a desirable physique

blocks.note: first meaning: a set of cans of beer sold together
second meaning: well-defined stomach muscles

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests beer gives you a good body, an irony since drinking tends to undo the toned stomach muscles of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a pack of six cans and the visible ridges of toned abdominal muscle.

clue.text: Judge a female beast of burden?

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey, used to carry loads
the suffix that makes a female form, as in lioness

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a female donkey has its own name.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: by analogy with lioness, a female donkey would be an ass-ess.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or appraise something, which is what it means to judge it.

clue.text: Distinctly cunning around stringed instrument

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for crafty is wrapped about the instrument

blocks.note: sly means crafty or cunning
a harp is a large instrument played by plucking strings

explanation.surface: A crafty musician plays clearly on a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharply can mean clearly and in a well-defined way, as in sharply contrasting, the same as distinctly.

clue.text: Standing in street, American receives thanks

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the abbreviation for street takes the thanks word inside it

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
ta is informal British for thank you
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American standing in the street is thanked by a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the street abbreviation does the receiving: the thanks word sits inside it before the American piece is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's status is their rank or position in society, which is also their standing.

clue.text: Extra time travelling around? This shows the fare

indicators.note: travelling around suggests moving about, so the letters before are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cab driver takes the long way, and the clock on the dashboard shows the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A taximeter is the device in a cab that calculates and displays the charge for the journey.

clue.text: Little kids grabbing tail of tree bears

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used
grabbing means seizing and holding, so the word for small children closes around the letter

blocks.note: tots are small children
the final letter of tree

explanation.surface: Small children clutch a toy bear or a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Bears looks like the animals, perhaps teddies; it is a verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something, and to bear something also means to carry it.

clue.text: Barman regularly scrubbed a couple of cups

indicators.note: removing at regular intervals leaves every other letter of the word

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of Barman

explanation.surface: A bartender routinely washes a pair of drinking cups.
explanation.walkthrough: Cups suggests drinkware for a barman; it means the two parts of an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: This undergarment has two shaped cups to support the breasts, hence a couple of cups.

clue.text: Promotional material Britpop band put on book

indicators.note: in a down entry, put on means placed above, so the band comes first and the book letter follows

blocks.note: Blur were a leading 1990s British pop band
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A 1990s band issues advertising material for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short description printed on a book cover to promote and sell it.

clue.text: Journey in trains running on time

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so the letters of the preceding word are set into a new order
on means placed next to, so the abbreviation for time is added after the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A trip by railway where the services run punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage from one place to another, which is what a journey is.

clue.text: Fruit — soft and fleshy

blocks.note: a plum is a stone fruit
p is short for piano, the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A description of a ripe piece of fruit: soft and juicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes something rounded and full-bodied, carrying a pleasant amount of flesh.

clue.text: Listener’s search for believer

indicators.note: a listener hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by sound and respelt

blocks.note: to seek is to search

explanation.surface: Someone tuned in hunts for a person of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sikh is a follower of Sikhism, the faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab.

clue.text: Rogue may bless parliament

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly and out of control, so the letters after it break their order

blocks.note: the eight letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel member might give a lawmaking chamber their blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a body of elected representatives that makes laws, as a parliament does.
